messages:
Sara (PM): FYI inbound from Mira re: MedEdge - they want guaranteed night & morning batch windows + daytime interactive chat. asking for committed capacity + burst buffer. can we size?
Mira (Account Exec): MedEdge expects predictable cost. they run large nightly ingestion (embeddings) 02:00-04:00 PT and peak chat 09:30-11:00 PT. estimate: nightly embedding peak ~18k embeddings/sec for 2 hours, daytime chat peak ~900 concurrent sessions, avg 0.5 rps, avg response 180 tokens. SLA: <300ms p95 for chat interactive.
Jules (Solutions Eng): Quick calc: chat token TPS ~900 * 0.5 * 180 = 81k tokens/sec. embeddings workload is separate and bursty; embeddings cost is heavy but throughput-friendly.
Ben (SRE): 81k token/s sustained at peak for chat is significant. on A100-80 we see ~20-30k token/s for 70B fp16 in our benchmarks under continuous batching. so ballpark 3-4 GPUs for chat alone if we keep that model.
Kai (Infra Eng): For embeddings, depending on model (embedding-1-large vs smaller quantized), throughput varies. If using a quantized 13B embedding model, a single GPU can hit ~30-40k embeddings/s. for 18k/s we could fit into 1 instance but need headroom and warmup.
Jules (Solutions Eng): Options to present to customer: 1) dedicated pool sized for daytime chat (4x A100), separate reserved embedding pool (1-2x smaller GPUs) + burst policy to use shared capacity for unexpected spikes; 2) combine into single pool with mixed-instance autoscaler and model routing. Recommend 1 for isolation.
Mira (Account Exec): They want price predictability. they'll accept a committed pool + measured burst credits. need guidance on cost delta for committing 4 GPUs vs 6 with burst buffer.
Sara (PM): From product POV we need launch criteria to move to proposal: 1) autoscale policy drafted 2) cost estimate for committed vs committed+burst 3) rollback/fallback model plan if peak > provisioned 4) test run with synthetic traffic.
Ben (SRE): Suggest autoscale policy draft: ````
min_replicas: 3
max_replicas: 8
scale_metric: token_rate
target_token_rate_per_replica: 22000
burst_multiplier: 2
burst_window: 10m
````
This keeps baseline low but allows short 2x bursts for 10 minutes.
Kai (Infra Eng): note: burst_multiplier uses shared pool - we must guarantee fallback path if shared capacity exhausted. fallback: route to quantized 70B-8bit or smaller 13B chat model with increased latency SLO p95 <700ms.
Jules (Solutions Eng): Add prefix/KV cache warmup during nightly embedding window to avoid first-request latency spikes for daytime chat. cache priming script can run at 01:45 PT.
Mira (Account Exec): Customer asks for a 99.9% uptime for daytime window and a billing model that caps burst charges per month. can we map this to draft SLA?
Sara (PM): We'll propose: SLA applies to committed pool only (p95 latency and uptime). Bursts are best-effort; we offer capped burst spend with monthly threshold and alerting. Need legal sign-off but OK to propose.
Ben (SRE): Also recommend canary for rollout: route 5% of traffic to dedicated pool for first 48h post-provision, monitor p95/p99 and error budget. if regressions, auto rollback to hosted variant.
Kai (Infra Eng): Ops note: provisioning time for 4x A100 reserved capacity ~24-48h depending on inventory. If they need faster, offer a staged plan: 2 reserved, 2 burst-capacity reserved for 2 weeks then convert.
Sara (PM): Action items: - Jules to produce detailed sizing spreadsheet + fallback model perf delta (due EOD Tues) - Kai to write autoscale + burst config snippet and provisioning ETA (due Wed) - Ben to draft rollout & canary checklist + test harness (due Wed) - Mira to align commercial ask (burst cap) and confirm customer's target sign-off date (due Mon)
Jules (Solutions Eng): Opening backlog ticket PROD-4209 with notes + link to this thread. will attach perf numbers and the cache priming script.
CapacityBot: automated note: Reserved capacity request template created (#REQ-8843). ETA: inventory check started.
Mira (Account Exec): thanks team. I'll loop in MedEdge legal on SLA framing and come back with their procurement timeline.
Sara (PM): Great, let's sync Thurs 10am PT after initial numbers. :thumbsup:
